title: Toxic week 2: Yash's film crawls to Rs 263 crore as 300-crore flop looms
excerpt: Yash's Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups added just Rs 6.75 crore in its second weekend, taking its 12-day India gross to Rs 263 crore. Trade trackers say the costly film is headed for one of the biggest losses in Indian cinema.
body:
• Yash's Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups grossed Rs 263 crore in India after 12 days, after adding just Rs 6.75 crore in its second weekend — a 96% fall from its opening weekend.
  • The film is on track to close its entire theatrical run under Rs 270 crore gross in India, well short of its costs, with losses expected to rank among the highest ever in Indian cinema.
  • The Hindi version, which carried the film early on, collapsed on its second Friday with a 75% drop to Rs 60 lakh; the English version was pulled from theatres after just seven days.
  • Directed by Geethu Mohandas and co-starring Kiara Advani, Nayanthara, Huma Qureshi and Tara Sutaria, the film opened huge on August 26 but sank under poor audience reception.

The theatrical run of Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups has effectively ended. Yash's much-hyped return to the big screen wrapped its second weekend with Rs 6.75 crore in India, taking its 12-day gross to Rs 263 crore, trade tracker Pinkvilla reported on September 7. With weekday collections crawling and screens fast disappearing, the film is expected to add only Rs 5-10 crore more and close its entire run around Rs 270-275 crore gross — a fraction of what a film of its scale and budget needed to break even.

The second-weekend number was down 96% from the opening weekend, one of the steepest second-week falls for a major Indian release this year. The Hindi version, which drove most of the film's business, managed just Rs 60 lakh on its second Friday — a 75% drop from the previous day — taking its 10-day Hindi total to Rs 128.60 crore. The film's English-language version, aimed at multiplex audiences, was withdrawn from theatres after only seven days when collections failed to pick up.

Context: a massive opening, then a cliff

Toxic, directed by Geethu Mohandas and produced by KVN Productions, released on August 26 with the full weight of Yash's KGF-era stardom behind it. It opened to a massive Rs 50.31 crore in Hindi alone on day one, grossing about Rs 153 crore across India in its first two days. But the fall began almost immediately: day two collections dropped 65% from opening day, with the Hindi version falling around 60% and Telugu states crashing by nearly 80%. Andhra Pradesh alone plunged by close to 90%, an almost unprecedented single-day decline.

The extended first week closed at Rs 256.25 crore gross, meaning the film has added less than Rs 10 crore across the whole of week two. Trade reports attributed the collapse to poor audience reception compounded by heavily front-loaded advance bookings that left little room for walk-in business. The Hindi version, expected to be the film's backbone, finished its first seven days at Rs 124.62 crore and was projected to close at Rs 135 crore nett — never even reaching triple its opening-day number.

Impact: the math that went wrong

Pinkvilla's trade analysis was blunt: Toxic is a failure at the box office, and worse at the financial level, with losses set to rank among the highest ever in Indian cinema. The costs were very high and, crucially, the film fumbled its non-theatrical recoveries — the digital, satellite and music rights that big-budget Indian films typically depend on to limit theatrical risk.

The South Indian markets were effectively a one-day run: after the opening, collections crashed everywhere except Karnataka, the star's home state, where some business persisted. In the North, the Hindi version held up slightly better in Gujarat and Odisha but faded everywhere else. The arrival of competing releases in week two, including the film Mirzapur and the breakout performance of Hanuman Ansh, squeezed out its remaining screens.

Diaspora angle

For diaspora audiences, Toxic's fate carries a familiar lesson from the star-driven era: record openings no longer guarantee legs when word of mouth turns. The film's English version — conceived partly for overseas and urban multiplex audiences — lasted barely a week, and its international prospects now rest on how the streaming window performs abroad.

What's next

With the theatrical run essentially over and the final gross likely to land under Rs 270 crore, attention shifts to the film's digital premiere and whether non-theatrical revenues can narrow the losses. For Yash, who carried the film's marketing on his shoulders, the underperformance of such an expensive project will shape the terms of his next outing. For the industry, it is another data point in the growing argument that budgets must follow audience response, not opening-weekend euphoria.
